icd10_codes.description: Colles' fracture of right radius, initial encounter for closed fracture
Fall on same level from slipping, tripping and stumbling without subsequent striking against object, initial encounter
Public park as the place of occurrence of the external cause

dialogue:
[doctor] good afternoon , mrs . {PATIENT_LAST} . is it okay if i call you {PATIENT_FIRST} ?
[patient] {PATIENT_FIRST} is fine . hi , doctor {DOCTOR_LAST} .
[doctor] so i understand you had a fall this morning ?
[patient] yes . i was out jogging in the park this morning , early , around six thirty . i go with my neighbor {OTHER_FIRST} three mornings a week , we do the loop around the pond at {PLACE} .
[doctor] okay .
[patient] and it was still a little dark under the trees , and i caught my toe on a tree root that was sticking up out of the path , and i tripped and went flying forward .
[doctor] oh , no .
[patient] and i put my right hand out to catch myself and landed on it , on the dirt path , and i felt it bend back and there was this awful pain .
[doctor] okay . so you landed on your outstretched right hand . did you hit anything else on the way down , a bench or a rock or anything ?
[patient] no , just the ground . i scraped my knees a little , but it's mostly my wrist .
[doctor] okay . did you hit your head ?
[patient] no .
[doctor] okay . and how does the wrist feel now ?
[patient] it's swollen and it looks kind of bent , like a fork . it really hurts if i try to move it . {OTHER_FIRST} drove me straight here .
[doctor] okay . on a scale of one to ten ?
[patient] about a seven . more if i move it .
[doctor] okay . any numbness or tingling in your fingers ?
[patient] my fingers feel a little bit tingly , but i can feel them .
[doctor] which fingers ?
[patient] kind of the thumb and the first two fingers .
[doctor] okay . we'll keep an eye on that . are you right handed ?
[patient] yes , unfortunately .
[doctor] okay . now , i see from your chart we've been treating your cholesterol . you're on atorvastatin ?
[patient] yes , twenty milligrams at night .
[doctor] okay . any muscle aches with it ?
[patient] no , i've been fine on it .
[doctor] good . your last lipid panel in the spring , your ldl was one twenty two , which was down from one sixty , so that's a good improvement .
[patient] oh , good .
[doctor] okay . have you ever had a bone density scan ?
[patient] i had one a few years ago and they said it was okay .
[doctor] okay . let me take a look at your wrist . i'm going to be gentle . so , looking at your right wrist , there is swelling and a dorsal angulation , what we call a dinner fork deformity . you're tender over the distal radius here . the skin is intact , no open wounds . i'm going to check your fingers . can you make an okay sign ? good . and spread your fingers ? good . your capillary refill is brisk and your radial pulse is present . you have slightly decreased light touch over the tip of the index finger , but otherwise sensation is intact . there's no tenderness in the snuffbox here , and your elbow is fine .
[patient] okay .
[doctor] you've got some superficial abrasions on both knees , they're clean .
[patient] okay .
[doctor] so we did x-rays of your wrist . hey dragon , show me the right wrist x-rays . so looking at these , you have a fracture at the end of the radius , about two centimeters above the joint , and the broken piece is tilted backward . this is what we call a colles' fracture . it does n't look like it goes into the joint , and the ulna is okay .
[patient] okay . so it's broken .
[doctor] yes . so for my assessment and plan , for the right wrist , you have a closed colles' fracture with dorsal angulation . because it's tilted back , we're going to do a closed reduction today , which means we numb the area with a hematoma block and pull it back into position , and then put you in a splint .
[patient] okay .
[doctor] after that we'll repeat the x-rays to make sure it's lined up . because of the tingling in your fingers , we'll recheck your sensation after the reduction , and that usually improves once the bone is back in place . you'll keep it elevated above your heart and ice it . for pain , you can take tylenol and i'll give you a few tablets of something stronger for night time .
[patient] okay .
[doctor] i'm going to refer you to hand orthopedics this week . sometimes these need surgery if they slip after reduction . you'll be in a cast for about six weeks .
[patient] okay . and the jogging ?
[doctor] no jogging until the cast is off and ortho clears you . walking is fine .
[patient] okay .
[doctor] and since you broke a bone from a fall from standing height , i want to repeat your bone density scan to make sure we're not missing osteoporosis .
[patient] that makes sense .
[doctor] for your cholesterol , continue the atorvastatin twenty milligrams . we'll recheck your lipid panel at your next physical .
[patient] okay . thank you .
[doctor] you're welcome . we'll get you set up for the reduction .
note:
CHIEF COMPLAINT

Right wrist injury.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS

{PATIENT_FIRST} {PATIENT_LAST} is a {AGE}-year-old right-hand-dominant female with hyperlipidemia who presents on {DATE_NUM} after a fall while jogging in a public park this morning. She caught her toe on a tree root on the path, tripped and fell forward onto her outstretched right hand on a dirt path. She did not strike any object and did not hit her head. She reports immediate pain and deformity of the right wrist, pain 7/10, and mild tingling of the thumb, index and middle fingers. She also has abrasions of both knees.

She takes atorvastatin 20 mg nightly for hyperlipidemia without myalgias. Most recent LDL was 122, improved from 160. Prior bone density scan reportedly normal.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION

Right wrist: Swelling with dorsal angulation (dinner fork deformity). Tenderness over the distal radius. Skin intact. No anatomic snuffbox tenderness. Elbow nontender.
Neurovascular: Capillary refill brisk. Radial pulse present. Slightly decreased light touch at the tip of the index finger, otherwise sensation intact. Motor function intact.
Skin: Superficial abrasions of the bilateral knees.

RESULTS

X-rays of the right wrist demonstrate an extra-articular distal radius fracture approximately 2 cm proximal to the articular surface with dorsal angulation, consistent with a Colles' fracture. Ulna intact.

ASSESSMENT

1. Closed Colles' fracture of the right radius after a trip and fall while jogging in a public park.
2. Mild median nerve paresthesias.
3. Hyperlipidemia.

PLAN

Closed reduction under hematoma block with sugar-tong splint today. Post-reduction x-rays and neurovascular recheck. Elevation, ice, Tylenol, short course of analgesic at night. Referral to hand orthopedics this week. No jogging until cleared. Repeat DEXA scan given fragility-type fracture. Continue atorvastatin 20 mg nightly; repeat lipid panel at next physical.
